commands.name: /start
commands.when: Once, on a fresh unpacked folder (context/identity.md still has {{ }} placeholders), and again to resume a first session that was broken off. After the folder is personal it no longer onboards — it says hello and hands over to /session-start.
commands.what_you_type: start (or /start) — CLAUDE.md:5 says 'Just type start'; README.md:40 says 'Type /start'
steps_for_the_person: ① It greets you, asks what to call you, and reads one paragraph of what is about to happen: three stories, ~15 minutes, a card per area to correct, then it builds the folder, and you can stop any time. It explicitly promises it will not ask you to rate yourself (start:61-78).
It takes your manner from your very first reply — language, how you address it, length, lists or prose, strong language — and holds it (start:37-49).

② One yes/no question: set up search by meaning? It states the cost honestly before you answer — ~300 MB downloaded once, ~1 GB on disk, 5-10 minutes. Yes → it runs the install in the background and carries on without making you wait; no → 'Fine, I'll search by exact words' (start:80-99).
Silently, saying nothing to you, it prepares the folder: starts keeping earlier versions of your notes and makes inbox/ (start:101-109).

③ Three stories, one per turn, in its own words, not as a list: yesterday from waking to sleep; the last month — what you bought, regret, are glad about; what you learned this year and from whom (start:112-124).
Each story is saved word for word; then for each area it shows a card and you correct it by number ('3 is wrong, what actually happened is…') (start:130-133, svoboda-profiler:230-257).
After at least two cards confirmed or corrected, it warns about the restart and builds your folder — you type no second command (start:135-142).

④ It tells you the three things you will actually use: just talk to me; drop your day in (words or inbox/); say 'save this'. Then asks you once to close it and open it again in the same folder — the only thing you do by hand in the whole session (start:152-166).
what_it_writes: git repo initialised if absent (git init -q) — start:105

then everything vault-scaffolder writes (CLAUDE.md, context/identity.md, context/root.md, context/goals.md, HOME.md, MEMORY.md, knowledge/people/{id}.md, knowledge/moc/MOC_people.md, state/current.md) — start:142
.memory_venv/ + state/memory-index/nodes.npz, if you said yes to search by meaning (bootstrap.sh:19-30)
commands.what_you_see: Plain conversation only. No program output, no paths, no errors, no logs — 'one plain sentence instead' (start:177). Cards read aloud as numbered lines, then 'I don't know', then 'I heard X — right?', then its own reading of the area last (svoboda-profiler:230-251).
commands.plain_words_alternative: None needed — this is the one command. The hook itself tells the assistant to run it if your first message is 'start' or '/start' (session-start.sh:23).

commands.name: /session-start
commands.when: Beginning a working session, or when context needs a fresh boot. In practice the SessionStart hook already does this at every launch; the skill is the manual fallback for a subagent, another entry point, or a failed hook.
commands.what_you_type: /session-start — but you normally never type it: the hook runs at every launch (session-start.sh:2, CLAUDE.md:28)
steps_for_the_person: Step 0: it checks whether the start hook already poured in the '--- State ---' block; if so it skips re-reading those files to save budget (session-start:13).

If state/current.md is absent or identity.md still has {{ }}: it says ONE plain line in your language — 'This folder isn't set up yet — just type start and I'll do the rest' — and stops. It never writes the word 'vault' to you (session-start:15-19).
Otherwise it reads current state, priorities, the live anti-pattern watch-list, today's daily note, and any session checkpoints (session-start:20-24).

It shows a compact dashboard in plain words, in your language, with no paths and no jargon: in focus now / where we stopped / what I remember not to repeat / today / can be continued (session-start:28-42).
Then asks 'What are we working on?' if it isn't obvious (session-start:50).
what_it_writes: Nothing — read-only boot (no write step in the skill)
commands.what_you_see: A five-line dashboard in your own language, or the one-line 'not set up yet' notice.
commands.plain_words_alternative: Just open the folder and say hello — the hook does this on its own at every launch.

commands.name: /session-save
commands.when: At the end of a conversation worth keeping, or when the conversation has got heavy (the skill says >150K tokens; CLAUDE.md:45 sets the working ceiling at 100K). Not for trivial sessions (session-save:96).
steps_for_the_person: It first re-reads this conversation as friction data: where you corrected it, what you valued, where it missed or added noise (session-save:16).

If you corrected HOW it talks to you ('shorter', 'don't ask me that', 'use my first name'), it shows you one or two candidate lines for the 'How to work with me' section of your own file and writes down only what you agreed to — silence is not agreement (session-save:18-23).

If something new about one of the seven areas came up in passing, your verbatim phrase goes into stories/additions.md and ONE line into that area's card; the number for the area is not recalculated and the card is not shown again (session-save:25-41).
It summarises everything not yet written down since the last commit — not just the last task — and explicitly hunts for orphaned work that exists only in the transcript (session-save:43-48).
Genuinely new, reusable knowledge gets its own page in knowledge/ with [[wikilinks]] (session-save:50-52).
It updates where-we-stopped and appends 2-3 lines to today's note (session-save:54-56).
It writes a checkpoint file you can resume from, under 500 words (session-save:62-81, 95).
It commits to git (initialising the repo first if there isn't one), after checking nothing heavy or external is about to be committed (session-save:83-90).
If the tidy-up or the misses review was due this session and hasn't been done, it offers it now in ONE sentence and runs it only on your yes (session-save:92).
what_it_writes: context/identity.md § 'How to work with me' — 0-2 dated lines, only what you agreed to
memory/svoboda/{id}/domains/{area}.md — max two lines per session
HOME.md — one line when an area gets its first entries
context/anti-patterns.md / context/learned.md — if anything was triggered or learned
.gitignore — if something heavy was found untracked
commands.what_you_see: A short report of what was saved, plus the one-or-two candidate 'how to work with me' lines for your yes or no.

commands.name: /recall
commands.when: You want an old note back and you no longer remember the words you wrote it in; or the assistant doesn't remember earlier context.
steps_for_the_person: Step 0, before anything else: it checks with one pre-allowed `ls` whether search by meaning is actually installed here, so you never see an 'allow this?' window (recall:13-19).
Both parts present → it searches by meaning and gives you a ranked list of candidate files with the matching section and a snippet (recall:54-61).
Either part missing → it does NOT launch the engine (you would get an error full of paths). It searches by exact words instead, trying 2-3 word forms before saying nothing was found (recall:20-31).

In that case it tells you once per conversation, in one plain line: 'Search by meaning isn't installed here — I'm searching by exact words. Say the word if you want it on.' Not one word to you about venvs, models or gigabytes (recall:32-38).
Engine present but fell over → it goes quietly into the exact-words branch; the conversation never stops because of search (recall:39-41).
The result is a set of candidates, not the answer: it then opens the top 1-3 files and reads the section (recall:62).
what_it_writes: Nothing — read-only. (Only the optional install, on your explicit yes, writes .memory_venv/ and state/memory-index/nodes.npz)
commands.what_you_see: The found note, read back to you. Score ≥0.5 is usually an exact hit; 0.4-0.5 gets eyeballed (recall:60-61).
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'find where I wrote about…' (README.md:86), 'where did I write about being tired in the mornings' (docs/en/presentation.md:72)

commands.name: /reflect
commands.when: Every ~3 days. The start hook measures it and offers it to you in one sentence ('Shall I go over the misses of the last few days?'); it runs only on your yes. You may also ask for it yourself at any time.
steps_for_the_person: It gathers the last 3-5 daily notes, recent decisions, the anti-pattern watch-list, past lessons and the recent git log (reflect:19-24).

The main signal is the conversation itself: it reads recent session transcripts from Claude Code's own projects directory — narrowly, extracting only your turns, its replies and the friction points, never bulk-loading (reflect:26-38).
About you: how you responded, what you valued or disliked, what latent needs surfaced → candidates for your identity file, each tagged with where it came from (reflect:39).

About itself: where it landed, where it substituted its own agenda, where it failed to orient, over-produced or made you wait — each real friction point becomes an anti-pattern candidate (reflect:40).
It analyses patterns, extracts lessons, proposes concrete improvements, and reviews whether your goals still hold (reflect:42-64).
It writes a compact reflection report and commits it (reflect:66-76).
It stamps the run so the hook knows when the next one is due (reflect:90-93).
what_it_writes: context/anti-patterns.md — new anti-patterns (escalated to rules/ if the same mistake appears 3+ times, reflect:89)
state/last_reflect.txt — the stamp that closes the gate
commands.what_you_see: A compact honest report: patterns, learnings, improvements, stats. 'Be honest. Don't sugarcoat failures' (reflect:86).
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'go over the misses of the last few days' — and it offers this itself every ~3 days; you only say yes or later (README.md:84-86).

commands.name: /dream
commands.when: Dual gate, both must be true: ≥24h since the last tidy-up AND ≥5 sessions since. You never compute this and never type the word: the start hook prints '💤 Memory tidy-up is due' and the assistant offers it to you in ONE sentence in your language; it runs only on your yes. 'The person never needs to know the word dream' (dream:127-133).
commands.what_you_type: Nothing. You answer yes to the offer. (The command itself is /dream and a direct request in any words overrides the gate — dream:141.)
steps_for_the_person: Phase 1 — it first looks at what is already in memory before writing anything. 'If you skip Phase 1, abort the dream' (dream:35-46).
Phase 2 — it gathers recent signal: daily logs, facts that have drifted out of date, triggered anti-patterns, reflection reports, narrow transcript greps, semantic contradictions (dream:48-62).

Phase 3 — it merges its own repeated notes into the existing files instead of leaving near-copies, converts 'yesterday'/'last week' into real dates, and deletes facts it has since found wrong (dream:64-79).
Phase 4 — it shortens its own table of contents (MEMORY.md) back under 200 lines and 25KB, removing stale pointers (dream:81-97).
Phase 5 — it refreshes search by meaning, re-embedding only the changed files (seconds, not the ~35-minute full build). Skipped without a word if search by meaning isn't installed (dream:99-111).
Phase 6 — it closes the gate, then reports in ≤15 lines what it changed (dream:113-123).
Your own words — the stories you told it — are not touched, and earlier versions of the files are kept (docs/en/presentation.md:66).
what_it_writes: state/memory-index/nodes.npz — refreshed (full write + atomic replace, never an incremental upsert)
state/last_dream.txt and state/session_count_since_dream.txt — the two commands that close the gate (dream:135-139)
commands.what_you_see: One sentence asking permission, then a few lines afterwards saying what it changed. If nothing changed, one line saying so (dream:121).
commands.plain_words_alternative: You say yes to 'My memory needs a few minutes of tidying — do it now?' (CLAUDE.md:29). Asking for a tidy-up in any words also works.

commands.name: /compress
commands.when: The conversation is getting heavy and has to be handed to a fresh session; or you paste text/point at a file and want it shortened without losing facts.
steps_for_the_person: It applies all five techniques at once — structural (prose→tables, bullets), linguistic (kill filler and hedging, active voice), symbolic (→ | + = ✓/✗ ~), abbreviation, deduplication — to roughly 30% of the original (compress:10-42).
For /compress context it reviews the whole conversation, extracts goals/decisions/progress/pending/files and outputs a handoff blob under 2KB with the ratio shown (compress:46-48).
It then verifies: every file path exact, every number kept, every name kept, meaning recoverable by someone who never read the original (compress:56-62).

Advisory trigger: as the main thread nears the 100K ceiling, or when /session-save is invoked, compress first; when clearly heavy it compresses, saves, refuses further execution and hands over the blob (compress:64-66).
what_it_writes: Nothing by itself — it returns compressed text (a blob) for a new session
commands.what_you_see: The compressed text plus the compression ratio.

commands.name: /enable-modules
commands.when: You (or the assistant) flipped a module's enabled: true in modules.yaml and want it installed. Also to prune modules you turned off.
steps_for_the_person: It reads modules.yaml at the folder root; if the file is absent it says so and stops (enable-modules:28).

For each module marked enabled: true it copies modules/<name>/SKILL.md into .claude/skills/<skill>/, copies references/ if present, makes the declared folders, and copies the starter files — but only where the destination does not already exist, so it never clobbers anything you filled in (enable-modules:33-37).
It prints the module's human precondition line as a reminder, never enforcing it (enable-modules:37, 66).
--prune removes .claude/skills/<skill>/ for modules marked enabled: false, and nothing else, ever (enable-modules:39, 64).
--dry-run prints the plan and changes nothing (enable-modules:68).
Re-running is safe — idempotent overwrite (enable-modules:9, 62). It never edits modules.yaml for you; you flip enabled: by hand (enable-modules:69).
what_it_writes: the folders listed under dirs: in modules.yaml
the seed files listed under seeds: — only if the destination doesn't exist
commands.what_you_see: One line per module: installed | pruned | skipped | already-present, plus any seed warnings (enable-modules:40).
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'turn on that extra skill' / 'install the module'

commands.name: /graph-add
commands.when: A new person, project, concept, tool, decision, research note or business entity needs a page of its own in the notes.
steps_for_the_person: It works out the type, the name and the key facts, asking only for whatever you didn't give it (graph-add:26-28).

Conflict check first: if an existing note already asserts a different value for the same thing, it does NOT overwrite — it files a conflict record with both claims and their provenance, marks the original disputed, then stops and tells you (graph-add:29).
It searches for related existing notes, creates the new page with frontmatter and [[wikilinks]], then adds a backlink in at least one related file (graph-add:34-50).
It validates that the new page actually has an incoming link — a page nothing links to is invisible, and that is the #1 graph quality rule (graph-add:60, 65-74).
It reports what was created and what it linked to (graph-add:51).
what_it_writes: a backlink added to ≥1 existing related file
commands.what_you_see: What was created and what it was linked to.
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'write a page about this person / this project', 'remember this as its own note'

commands.name: /ingest
commands.when: A raw source — a transcript, a YouTube video, a chat export, notes, a survey — needs turning into pages in your notes.
commands.what_you_type: /ingest [source_type] [path] [topic] — source types: telegram | transcript | youtube | notes | bio | survey | audio
steps_for_the_person: Phase 1: it detects the source type; for a YouTube URL it makes inbox/youtube/{slug}_{video_id}/ and fetches the auto-subtitles with yt-dlp (which must be installed). If no subtitle file comes back it does NOT fabricate a transcript — it marks the source unresolved and asks you to paste one (ingest:20).
It splits the source into ~1500-token chunks and runs parallel subagents over five dimensions: biographical facts, behaviour patterns, values, people/relationships, insights (ingest:23-29).

Phase 2: it deduplicates, consolidates, and creates or updates pages in knowledge/ with resolving [[wikilinks]] and epistemic frontmatter. Anything under 0.5 confidence is marked uncertain and gets no page (ingest:35-42, 50, 57).
On a contradiction it files a conflict record rather than overwriting (ingest:56).

Phase 3: it reports how many pages it created or updated, updates where-we-stopped, and appends to today's note. Every processed source gets one coverage line — covered / omitted_boilerplate / redacted / unresolved — and any unresolved blocks completion (ingest:44-48, 58).
commands.what_you_see: A summary of entities created/updated, key findings, and the coverage table.
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'read this transcript into my notes', 'take a look in inbox'

commands.name: /lint
commands.when: Weekly, or after a big ingest session — a periodic health check that stops the notes rotting.
steps_for_the_person: Floating nodes: pages nothing links to, resolved through aliases. Target zero, fix immediately (lint:20-63, 196).
Stale claims: pages whose last_verified is older than 30 days (lint:66-87).
Contradictions: the same recurring number claimed differently in different pages (lint:89-98).
Missing cross-references: a name mentioned without a [[link]] to it (lint:100-108).
Source drift: pages whose recorded source hash no longer matches the source file (lint:110-131).
CLAUDE.md size: warns above 3500 bytes (limit 4000) (lint:133-137).
Index freshness: optional, only if you wired your own generator script — this starter ships none (lint:139-145).
Conflict integrity + epistemic enum validation: open conflicts awaiting resolution, and disputed notes with no matching conflict record (lint:147-165).
It prints a scored dashboard with a health score and a numbered ACTIONS list, most critical first (lint:167-192).
what_it_writes: Nothing by itself — it reports. Stale claims are escalated to you to verify; contradictions are escalated to you to resolve (lint:197-198)
commands.what_you_see: A boxed LINT report: floating nodes, stale claims, contradictions, missing cross-refs, source drift, CLAUDE.md size, index freshness, health score, actions.
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'check my notes are healthy', 'are any of my notes orphaned'

commands.name: /query
commands.when: A non-trivial question that needs synthesis across 2+ of your notes and that you would not want to re-derive next time. NOT for factual lookups or trivia — those are a grep (query:15-25).
steps_for_the_person: It searches whether this question, or a close variant, is already filed, and decides whether to augment, supersede or just refer you to it (query:29-35).
It gathers sources — domain hub pages first, then by tag, concept, person, and relevant reports — and lists them explicitly, because every claim needs a source (query:37-45).
It answers direct first, cites each claim to its source page, flags contradictions explicitly and quantifies uncertainty (query:47-53).
It scores its own answer against the quality gate (≥80/100) and iterates if it falls short (query:55-56).
It files the synthesis as a new page so the next similar question starts from it rather than from zero (query:58-83, 97).
It adds backlinks in each source so the new page isn't floating (query:85-86).
what_it_writes: backlinks appended to each source page
a log line with the question, the new path, the score and the source count
commands.what_you_see: The direct answer first, the evidence with citations, the caveats, and where it filed the answer.
commands.plain_words_alternative: Ask the question and add 'write this down' / 'file the answer'

commands.name: /self-check
commands.when: Checking the overall health of the folder or diagnosing what is missing.
steps_for_the_person: Nine layers each scored 0-2: CLAUDE.md, the knowledge graph (entity count, wikilink coverage, floating nodes), projects, skills, state freshness, the daily-notes streak, hooks, self-improvement entries, git health (self-check:13-142).
A fresh folder with no projects/ scores N/A on that row and it is dropped from the denominator — 'a blank vault is healthy-by-design here' (self-check:71).
It prints a boxed dashboard with the total score out of 16 (or 14), then GAPS highest-impact-first, each gap carrying a specific command to fix it (self-check:144-173, 182).
Health bands: 0-5 setup needed · 6-10 growing · 11-14 solid · 15-16 peak (self-check:169-173).
commands.what_you_see: A boxed SELF-CHECK dashboard with per-layer scores, a total, and a numbered gap list.
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'is anything broken in this folder?', 'how healthy is my setup'

commands.name: /svoboda-profiler
commands.when: The engine behind the first session — /start hands over to it. Also used later to re-do one area, to log a single drift fact, or to re-cut the portrait. You would normally never type it.
commands.what_you_type: /svoboda-profiler {subject_id} · … status · … synthesize · … scaffold · … update {domain} · … delta "{fact}" · … resynthesize (svoboda-profiler:42-50)
steps_for_the_person: Phase 0 — three stories instead of a questionnaire. You are never asked to rate yourself: 'this is the only place such a question is mentioned at all, and it is mentioned as a ban' (svoboda-profiler:90-94). Every story is saved word for word (svoboda-profiler:108-111).

Phase 1 — for each of the seven areas: it asks in one pass, writes a card with four kinds of line (your exact words / seen in your files / I think / I heard — right?), runs the quote check, then reads the card to you and you correct by number (svoboda-profiler:145-257).

The quote check is mandatory before any card is shown: any 'you said' line it cannot find verbatim in your own stories is rewritten as 'I heard: … — right?', and a failed run means the card is NOT shown (svoboda-profiler:207-221).
Your correction is appended verbatim to your stories FIRST, then the card is edited — otherwise the check pushes your fresh words straight back into a question (svoboda-profiler:253-257).
A plain 'yes' confirms only the 'you said' lines; its conclusions stay guesses until you answer them by number. Silence is not confirmation (svoboda-profiler:259-264).
Coverage under 40% → no number at all, 'you didn't talk about this' — not a zero and not 'a weak area' (svoboda-profiler:199-201).

Phase 2 (after 5+ areas) — 13 deeper layers, measurement not therapy: anger, losses, loneliness, irreversibility, attachment, attribution, rumination, boundary under pressure, time, strengths vs skills, mode under load (svoboda-profiler:333-351).
Phase 3 — parents and origin, optional (svoboda-profiler:353-357).
Phase 4 — synthesis. First run threshold is ≥2 confirmed cards → provisional portrait; a full pass wants 5 areas + 3 layers (svoboda-profiler:359-373).

Phase 4b — it scores its OWN work against the gate, never you; below 80 it iterates at most twice then accepts as provisional, and never tells you the session was 'too guarded' (svoboda-profiler:478-491).
Phase 4d — the dashboard / plan-vs-fact / plans files are created ONLY if you explicitly ask, and never pre-filled with its own numbers (svoboda-profiler:501-562).
Between sessions: one drift fact at a time (delta) accrues, and after ~3 it flags that area for a re-cut — a versioned diff, never a from-scratch rewrite (svoboda-profiler:573-589).
what_it_writes: memory/svoboda/{id}/stories/<area>.md, stories/corrections.md, stories/additions.md — your words verbatim
memory/svoboda/{id}/prefill.md — only on a repeat pass with lots of material
memory/svoboda/{id}/pp.md, plan-fact.md, plans.md — only on your explicit ask
commands.what_you_see: Cards read aloud: numbered lines, then 'I don't know', then 'I heard X — right?', then its reading of the area with how sure it is — as the last line, never the opening (svoboda-profiler:230-251).
commands.plain_words_alternative: 'let's go through this area again' → it re-cuts one area (session-save:41). 'profile me', 'unpack me'.

commands.name: /vault-scaffolder
commands.when: A finished profile.yaml exists and the blank folder needs turning into your folder. /start calls it for you; you type no second command.
steps_for_the_person: Gate first, before step one: it reads cards_confirmed and refuses to build on fewer than two areas you have seen and confirmed or corrected — 'the gate is not bypassed by an argument or by "just build it"'. It says so in ordinary words and shows you the next card instead (vault-scaffolder:33-42).
Two cards are the whole threshold of a first run: the folder is built in full, marked provisional, and depth accrues afterwards (vault-scaffolder:44-47).
It slugifies your id to [a-z0-9_-] for filenames while keeping your real display name as a title (vault-scaffolder:133).

Fill-in-place, not flatten: identity.md, MEMORY.md, HOME.md and goals.md ship as richer templates and get filled section by section; only CLAUDE.md is a genuine overwrite of the blank onboarding stub (vault-scaffolder:126, 143-145).

Your own file (context/identity.md) is written in the language you write in, in ordinary words, and your hand edits are preserved — a line you crossed out is never restored, a line you fixed is never rewritten (vault-scaffolder:228-238, 403-404).

'Where to invest' only lists areas you yourself named as a gap, in your own words. Its own low number never goes there — it stays in that area's card as its reading, for you to disagree with (vault-scaffolder:288, 405).

Re-run safety: your goals are preserved verbatim, existing where-we-stopped is skipped, profile anti-patterns are replaced in one delimited block instead of duplicated, existing operational files are skipped (vault-scaffolder:127, 289, 297, 330-332, 351).
It never regenerates the shipped anti-patterns or lessons corpus — it appends (vault-scaffolder:12, 291-293).
It finishes by telling you to restart Claude Code in this folder to activate (vault-scaffolder:382).
what_it_writes: CLAUDE.md — overwritten, personalized, must stay under 3500 bytes
HOME.md — filled in place, in your language
context/identity.md — filled in place, in your language, incl. § 'How to work with me'
context/root.md — §1 WHO, North Star, §3 domains filled; §2 and §4 untouched engine doctrine
context/goals.md — North Star + Domains to Develop refresh; Active Goals preserved
context/anti-patterns.md — APPENDED inside <!-- profile-aps:start/end -->; anti-patterns-index.md gets one 'profile' cluster row
folders: context knowledge/people knowledge/concepts knowledge/moc state daily reports scripts
commands.what_you_see: A plain-words result with no paths: 'I've built your folder: who you are — with your own words and my guesses kept separate; your goals; the area cards you have already seen; a front page with the seven areas… This is provisional… The files are ordinary files — open them and edit them' (start:146-150).

what_the_hook_pours_in: --- State --- : up to 40 non-blank lines of state/current.md, each cut to 400 chars, frontmatter stripped. Absent → '(no state/current.md yet — the first /session-save creates it)' (session-start.sh:65-72)

--- Priorities --- : the first '## ' section of context/priorities.md, up to 8 lines (title-agnostic on purpose, because a hard-coded title silently breaks when titles get renamed) (session-start.sh:74-83)
--- Today (YYYY-MM-DD) --- : the last 8 lines of today's daily note (session-start.sh:85-93)
--- Checkpoints --- : the 3 newest filenames in state/sessions/, newest first (session-start.sh:95-103)
--- boot: N bytes --- : the measured cost of everything it just printed (session-start.sh:155-157)
search-index drift sensor: 'search index is N commit(s) behind — /dream refreshes it'. Print only, never rebuilds (session-start.sh:105-115)
It also increments the session counter FIRST, before any printing, so a failing section cannot stop the count (session-start.sh:27-33)
at_every_start.gates: Two, and at most ONE offer per start — tidy-up first, reflection only if no tidy-up was offered (session-start.sh:159-162). 💤 Memory tidy-up is due: ≥24h since the last one AND ≥5 sessions since (session-start.sh:117-129). 🔍 Reflection is due: ≥3 days since the last one, baselined on when the folder was set up if there is no stamp yet (session-start.sh:131-144). Both print an instruction to the assistant, not to you: offer it in ONE sentence in the person's language and run only on a yes; never unasked, and never show the person the command names (CLAUDE.md:29).
at_every_start.before_onboarding: If context/identity.md is missing or still contains '{{', the hook prints ONE line and exits — nothing else. That line tells the assistant: if the person's first message is 'start' or '/start', run the start skill (it also resumes an interrupted first session); otherwise answer with ONE plain line in their language, 'This folder isn't set up yet — just type start and I'll do the rest.' And: 'Never say "vault" to the person.' (session-start.sh:21-25)

0b. Anything new about one of the seven areas → verbatim phrase into stories/additions.md under a dated heading, then ONE line into that area's card; a note in HOME.md if the area got its first entries; the number is NOT recalculated and the card is NOT shown again (session-save:25-41)
1. Summarise ALL un-persisted work since the last commit, scanning for orphans first — work done before a /compact is the likeliest orphan (session-save:43-48)
2. Extract genuinely new reusable knowledge into knowledge/ with [[wikilinks]] (session-save:50-52)
3. Update state/current.md and append 2-3 lines to daily/{today}.md (session-save:54-56)

at_save.how_to_work_with_me_lines: If during the session you corrected HOW it talks to you — 'shorter', 'don't ask me about that', 'use my first name', 'not as a list' — that is interface data, not a conclusion about you. 0-2 lines go into the 'How to work with me' section of context/identity.md, each with a date and your own words. No second such list is started in another file. It shows the candidates in ONE line and writes down only what you agreed with: 'silence is not agreement'. Conclusions about you (area cards, the profile) do not go here, and vice versa. (session-save:18-23; the section is the single source of truth per svoboda-profiler:315-319, 329-331)

tidy_up.gate: Dual gate, both must be true: ≥24h since the last tidy-up (state/last_dream.txt) AND ≥5 sessions since (state/session_count_since_dream.txt, counted by the start hook). The assistant does not compute it — the hook prints '💤 Memory tidy-up is due' and it offers it in one sentence; only a yes runs it. A direct request in any words overrides the gate, and still closes it afterwards. (dream:127-141, session-start.sh:117-129)
steps: Phase 1 Orient (mandatory) — list knowledge/ context/ state/, read MEMORY.md and where-we-stopped, skim the existing files in the area about to be touched, review recent checkpoints, and use search by meaning to surface related notes. 'Synthesis without prior reading = hallucination factory.' Skip this and the whole run aborts. (dream:35-46)

Phase 2 Gather — daily logs for the last 3-7 days, facts that have drifted against git, recently triggered anti-patterns, reflection reports, narrow transcript greps (never whole files), semantic contradictions (dream:48-62)

Phase 3 Consolidate — merge into existing topic files rather than creating near-duplicates; convert 'yesterday'/'last week' to absolute dates; delete facts today disproved rather than leaving both versions; every [[wikilink]] must resolve or the write is rejected by the hook (dream:64-79)

Phase 4 Prune and index — MEMORY.md back under 200 lines AND 25KB; remove stale/superseded pointers, demote verbose lines into their topic file, add newly important pointers, resolve contradictions rather than indexing both (dream:81-97)

Phase 5 Refresh search by meaning — re-embed only the changed files (seconds, not the ~35-minute full build). Skipped without a word if .memory_venv/bin/python is absent. Full-write + atomic replace only; the warm server re-reads by mtime on its own, so nothing needs killing (dream:99-111)
Phase 6 Report — close the gate first, then a brief ≤15-line summary: counts, top 3 merges or contradictions resolved, index size before→after, anything notable surfaced (dream:113-123)
tidy_up.what_it_never_touches: Your own words. 'Your own words — the stories you told it — are not touched, and earlier versions of the files are kept, so anything can be brought back' (docs/en/presentation.md:66). It also must not: skip Phase 1, read full transcripts, create near-duplicate files, leave two contradicted facts intact, dump content into MEMORY.md, or use any external API — local only (dream:143-150).
tidy_up.closes_with: Two commands, mandatory — skip them and the offer repeats at every start: `date +%s > state/last_dream.txt` and `echo 0 > state/session_count_since_dream.txt` (dream:135-139)

search.with_index: Node-level semantic search: one node per markdown section with the header path baked in, EmbeddingGemma-300m q8 ONNX at 768 dimensions, one .npz file of vectors, brute-force numpy cosine. No database, no external API. `.memory_venv/bin/python scripts/memory_index.py search "question"` returns rank / score / relative path / § header-path / snippet — a set of candidates to open, not the answer. Score ≥0.5 is usually an exact hit, 0.4-0.5 gets eyeballed. Indexed wings: knowledge/ daily/ context/ reports/ state/ memory/ inbox/ projects/ — which includes your verbatim stories and anything you drop in inbox/. (recall:43-66, memory_index.py:4-27, 55)
search.without: Exact-word grep across knowledge/ daily/ memory/ inbox/ state/ reports/, trying 2-3 word forms before saying nothing was found. The assistant checks first with a pre-allowed `ls` whether the engine exists and does NOT launch it when it doesn't, so you never see an error full of paths; it tells you once per conversation in one plain line and says nothing about venvs, models or gigabytes. Same quiet fallback if the engine is present but falls over. (recall:13-41)
search.install: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh` — offered once during onboarding as a yes/no question with the cost stated up front, and otherwise only on your explicit ask. It calls scripts/memory_index_setup.sh (python3 -m venv .memory_venv, then pip install numpy onnxruntime transformers huggingface_hub sentencepiece) and then builds the index. Every failure path is one plain line and exit 0 — no Python, no prebuilt wheels for this Python version, or an unfinished model download all end with 'Everything else works: notes are searched by exact words.' Onboarding never stops over it. (bootstrap.sh:1-32, memory_index_setup.sh:1-30, start:80-99)
search.size_and_where: ~309 MB model downloaded once, cached under ~/.cache/huggingface (outside the folder). The venv .memory_venv/ is ~1 GB and lives INSIDE the folder. The vectors are state/memory-index/nodes.npz plus manifest.json, inside the folder. All of it is gitignored and all of it is rebuildable without losing a single note — losing the venv loses no data, only the runtime. (memory_index_setup.sh:5-9, 29-30; memory-embedding-layer.md:100, 113; .gitignore:8-11)
search.warm_server: Not a daemon — a cache with a TTL. HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8765, stdlib only, model + vectors held in RAM (~500 MB). `search` knocks on it first; no server → it searches cold (~7s for the model load) and spawns the server in the background for next time (~65 ms thereafter). It dies on its own after 30 minutes idle, is read-only over the .npz, and re-reads the file by mtime after a rebuild — so nothing needs killing or restarting. If the port is already taken it exits quietly (a lazy-spawn race). (memory_index.py:22-26, 355-399; memory-embedding-layer.md:80; recall:43)

quote_check.what: scripts/check_quotes.py — standard library only, 'Sends nothing anywhere'. It takes every card line that starts with a 'you said' label and looks for it word for word in that person's saved stories folder (including stories/corrections.md, where their corrections land first). Comparison ignores case, punctuation, Russian ё and extra spaces. Not found → it prints the line number, shows was/now, and rewrites the line in place as 'I heard: … — right?' in the same language, meaning it was the assistant's wording and not the person's words. Usage: `python3 scripts/check_quotes.py memory/svoboda/{id}/domains/delo.md`, with --dry-run to show only and --stories to point elsewhere. Exit 0 = all quotes checked out; exit 1 = there were unverified lines, now flagged — DO NOT show the card, fix and re-run until clean in the same session; exit 2 = nothing to check (no stories, or the card has no quote line at all) — also 'do not show': save the story first, then build the card. No Python at all → the 'you said' lines are dropped from the showing entirely, leaving 'I saw in your files', 'I think' and 'I don't know': what is unverified is never passed off as the person's words. It is mandatory before any card is shown (svoboda-profiler Phase 1 Step D) and a precondition in start's own rules.
quote_check.labels: Three label sets, recognised by one regex: `you said:` (EN), `你说：` (ZH), `ты сказал:` / `ты сказала:` / `вы сказали:` (RU — the written-out `ты сказал(а):` is accepted too). The replacement text is language-matched: 'I heard: … — right?' / '我听到的是：…——对吗？' / 'я услышал: … — так?'. So a card written in any of the three is checked the same way and needs no rewriting before showing. (check_quotes.py:36-55; label table at svoboda-profiler:133-143 and start:24-31)

rules.one_line: The map of this folder: a hard rule is the backstop tier of a three-tier discipline mechanism (advisory anti-pattern → directive state → hard rule), and lands here only after the advisory layer demonstrably failed to stop a recurrence (rules/AGENTS.md:5-11).

Report the result, not a flattering frame around it — three mechanical prohibitions, escalated after the agent repeatedly reframed a weak result or a real failure as a wise choice and asserted the absence of things it simply hadn't checked (rules/honesty-register.md:4-14).

The engine assumes a local-only repo: git is a local snapshot convenience, not a contract with anyone — so plaintext credentials in tracked files, secrets in history, force-push/rotation advice, gitignore-for-secrets and backup infrastructure must NOT be raised as findings; only hygiene that affects how an agent operates may be (rules/local-only-repo.md:10-38).

Match the cost of the work to the scope of the task — a personal tool is a tool, not a product; escalated after over-engineering a local personal tool recurred a fifth time (rules/match-cost-to-scope.md:4-15).

Filenames are interface, not decoration: [a-z0-9_-] only, escalated after spaces, mixed case and non-ASCII caused cross-platform sync noise and case collisions more than once (rules/naming-convention.md:4-14).

Establish the frame BEFORE you commit to an answer, a fan-out or a build — the most expensive failures come from committing on an assumed frame rather than an established one (rules/orient-before-commit.md:4-14).

Don't ship an artifact judged by a sense the agent lacks — sight, sound, interaction — without perceiving it through a real proxy; escalated after shipping blind off 'it built OK' hit total rejection across several modalities (rules/perceive-before-ship.md:4-16).

Lead with a plain, demystified take — what it is and what it gives you, in ordinary language; never mirror the register of the source. Escalated after the operator disengaged ('too clever', 'I didn't understand any of it') (rules/plain-first.md:4-16).
Corrections are permanent and live infrastructure is read-only until asked — both failure modes share the root of not carrying durable state forward (rules/retain-corrections.md:4-13).

A password, PIN, key, token, card number, CVV, SMS code, wallet seed phrase or passport number is never carried into any file in the folder, even if the person dictated it — written specifically to close the gap between a promise made in the README and presentation and a neighbouring rule that read as permission (rules/secrets-never-in-notes.md:4-15).
Render the literal spec / answer the question asked, never the convenient nearby substitute — the most-cited failure class in the whole corpus (rules/substitution-instinct.md:4-14).

Whatever the operator designated as the primary work IS the work; other lanes are opt-in. Escalated after the agent kept redirecting toward a generic 'more valuable' goal because the bias was wired into a directive state file (rules/work-is-the-work.md:4-15).

modules: modules.yaml is the optional-modules manifest: everything off by default, file-based only, no DB, no registry, no daemons. Per module it declares enabled (install or not), skill (the install target .claude/skills/<skill>/), dirs (folders to create), seeds (starter files — destination is folder-relative, source is modules/<name>/seeds/<basename>, copied only when the destination doesn't already exist so user data is never clobbered), and requires (a human precondition the installer just prints, never enforces). The engine ships with NO modules of its own — only one worked example, example-skill, enabled: false, whose declared dir is reports/ and whose seed is reports/example-note.md: 'flip enabled:true and run /enable-modules to watch the mechanism work, then delete or replace this with your own'. /enable-modules does the mechanical copy (SKILL.md, references/, dirs, guarded seeds), is idempotent, supports --dry-run (print the plan, change nothing) and --prune (remove only .claude/skills/<skill>/ for disabled modules, never modules/ itself and never workspace dirs or seed data you filled in), warns rather than failing on a missing seed source or a stanza with no skill: field, and never edits modules.yaml for you — you flip enabled: by hand. Authoring one: copy modules/example-skill/ to modules/<yourname>/, edit, add a stanza, run /enable-modules. (modules.yaml:1-27 · .claude/skills/enable-modules/SKILL.md:9-69 · modules/example-skill/SKILL.md:10-22 · AGENTS.md:39)

history_and_backup.git: The folder keeps earlier versions of your notes in a local git repository. Bootstrap: /start runs `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || git init -q` quietly during onboarding, saying nothing to the person, because a folder unpacked from a downloaded ZIP carries no history — 'without this, saves have no history' (start:101-105). The same guard is repeated defensively in /session-save Step 6 and /reflect Step 7, so a missing repo is created on first use rather than failing. From then on each save commits '[session-save]: {summary}' and each misses review commits '[reflect]: {insight}' (session-save:86-89, reflect:72-76). Before `git add -A` the save inspects untracked weight and pushes heavy or external material into .gitignore instead of committing it, and never makes a source inaccessible while dropping its analysis in the same move (session-save:84-85). The start hook also uses git as a sensor: it compares the search index's recorded git_head against HEAD and prints how many commits behind it is (session-start.sh:105-115). By rule this git is 'a local snapshot convenience, not a contract with anyone' — no shared remote, no CI, no auditor assumed (rules/local-only-repo.md:14-18). NOTE: THIS working copy is not the shipped state — it has 37 commits and two real remotes (github → github.com/xcota/pos on main, gitee → gitee.com/cotya/pos-starter on master), because it is the maintainer's publishing checkout; a person who downloads the ZIP gets no .git at all, which is exactly why /start initialises one. RESTORE: no file, skill or doc in the folder documents a restore route — there is no `git log`/`git checkout`/`git revert` step anywhere for the person or the assistant, only the promise that 'earlier versions of the files are kept, so anything can be brought back' (docs/en/presentation.md:66, :141) and that git is 'the safety net of earlier versions of your notes'. The only recovery path actually written down is the manual one: 'move your old folder aside — your notes stay in it — unpack a fresh copy, and the assistant can bring your notes across' (docs/en/presentation.md:134).
history_and_backup.copy_move: 'Copy the folder and you have moved all your notes; delete the folder and the notes are gone' (README.md:68). Everything is ordinary text files on your own disk — no separate storage program, no server. Two things live OUTSIDE the folder and do not travel with it: Claude Code's own record of the conversations, kept in its service area (deleting your folder does not delete those), and the downloaded model cache for search by meaning under ~/.cache/huggingface (docs/en/presentation.md:108, :122). Both hooks and both python engines resolve their paths from their own file location or $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, never an absolute path, so 'the same wiring works from any copy regardless of where the folder lives' (semantic-recall.sh:8-9, memory_index.py:39-41, memory_index_setup.sh:8-9).
history_and_backup.reset: The rebuildable layers can be deleted and recreated without losing a note: `bash scripts/memory_index_setup.sh` recreates the ~1 GB venv (losing it 'loses NO data — nodes.npz + the model cache stay intact, only the runtime'), and `memory_index.py build` rebuilds the vector sidecar; both are gitignored by design so a blank clone ships without them (memory_index_setup.sh:4-6, memory-embedding-layer.md:100,113). bootstrap.sh is explicitly 'safe to re-run: the environment and the index are rebuilt from scratch, and the person's own notes are never touched' (bootstrap.sh:4-5). /enable-modules is idempotent. Re-running /vault-scaffolder does NOT reset your content: Active Goals are preserved verbatim, existing state/current.md is skipped, profile anti-patterns are replaced inside one delimited block rather than duplicated, existing pp.md/plan-fact.md/plans.md are skipped, and your hand edits and crossed-out lines in context/identity.md are never restored or rewritten (vault-scaffolder:127, 289, 297, 330-332, 351, 399, 403-404).

internet.what_goes_out: 1) Your conversation, including the pieces of your notes the assistant reads, goes to Anthropic's servers — 'the same as any text you type into an AI chat. Storage is on your side, thinking happens on Anthropic's servers. That is why you need an internet connection' (README.md:74, docs/en/presentation.md:112). The tidy-up is done by the assistant itself, so those notes go to Claude like anything else you write to it (presentation:112). 2) ONLY if you say yes to search by meaning: a one-off ~309 MB model download from Hugging Face (`hf_hub_download` of onnx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-ONNX, cached under ~/.cache/huggingface) plus pip installs of numpy, onnxruntime, transformers, huggingface_hub and sentencepiece into .memory_venv. Nothing is downloaded quietly — the cost is stated before you answer (memory_index.py:44-46,150-153; memory_index_setup.sh:25-30; start:80-87). 3) /ingest on a YouTube URL calls yt-dlp, which must already be installed (ingest:20). 4) publish.sh pushes to GitHub and Gitee — maintainer-only, not part of using the folder (publish.sh:29-40). No paid external API is required for anything, and the assistant is told not to use external APIs for memory work at all: 'Use external APIs — local only' (dream:150), 'Zero DB, zero external APIs' (recall:43), 'No MCP / external APIs / $0' (memory-embedding-layer.md:98).
internet.what_stays_local: The search engine and the quote check never leave your machine. The warm server binds 127.0.0.1:8765 only, holds the vectors in RAM, is read-only over the .npz and dies after 30 minutes idle — 'The only thing that ever runs in the background is the local search, if you turned it on — it wakes for your question and goes back to sleep after half an hour, on your machine' (presentation:106, memory_index.py:355-356, memory-embedding-layer.md:80). check_quotes.py is standard-library-only and 'Sends nothing anywhere' (check_quotes.py:25). The semantic-recall hook is vault-scoped only (semantic-recall.py:10). Your notes themselves are plain text files on your own disk with no storage program and no server of ours, and there is no account to create anywhere (README.md:68). Passwords, PINs, keys, card numbers, codes and recovery phrases are never written into any file even if you dictate one — a hard rule, not a promise (rules/secrets-never-in-notes.md:10-15, presentation:110).

contradictions: THE FULL GUIDE DOES NOT EXIST. README.md:88 links [docs/en/guide.md](docs/en/guide.md) and https://xcota.github.io/pos/en/guide.html; README.zh.md:90 and docs/ru/README.md:88 do the same for zh/ru; all three presentations point at it (docs/en/presentation.md:102, ru:102, zh:104 and the three .html files); docs/index.html:40 links en/zh/ru guide.html. Verified: docs/en/ contains only onboarding-flow.md, presentation.html, presentation.md — no guide.md in any language. The index page's own links even carry `?v=unpublished` (docs/index.html:40) while the presentation links carry a real build hash, so the page itself knows the guide was never published.

CLAUDE.md IS OVER ITS OWN SIZE LIMIT. Actual: 4428 bytes (verified `wc -c CLAUDE.md`). lint/SKILL.md:135-136 warns above 3500 ('limit 4000, safety 3500'); self-check/SKILL.md:61 says 'must be < 3500 chars'; vault-scaffolder/SKILL.md:145 states 'The blank onboarding stub ships at 3617B' and :392 warns 'Claude Code truncates at ~4000 silently'. So the shipped blank stub is 811 bytes larger than the file that describes it and 428 bytes past the stated truncation risk, and /lint and /self-check will both flag it on a fresh folder.

SELF-CHECK SAYS THE FOLDER SHIPS NO HOOKS. self-check/SKILL.md:109 scopes hooks to the GLOBAL ~/.claude/settings.json and states 'A fresh vault ships zero hooks, so 0/2 is correct by design'; its Step 7 command reads ~/.claude/settings.json only. But this folder ships .claude/settings.json:35-68 with three registered hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse), all three scripts present in .claude/hooks/ — and CLAUDE.md:28 treats the start hook as load-bearing. /self-check will under-report the folder's own machinery.

REFLECT SAYS ITS PERIODIC TRIGGER ISN'T SHIPPED. reflect/SKILL.md:15: 'Auto: wire up a periodic trigger yourself (e.g. a cron job or /loop calling /reflect) — not shipped by default.' But session-start.sh:131-143 ships exactly that gate (≥3 days, baselined on the folder's setup date) and prints '🔍 Reflection is due'; reflect's own Step 7 stamp (reflect:90-93) exists to feed it, and README.md:64 and presentation:68 promise the offer to the person. The line is stale.

THE .NPZ IS DESCRIBED AS BEING IN GIT AND IS GITIGNORED. memory_index.py:10 ('storage = ONE .npz sidecar in git') and :10-12 build the whole design argument on that. But .gitignore:10-11 excludes state/memory-index/*.npz and manifest.json, and memory-embedding-layer.md:100 states the opposite outright: 'The venv and every .npz are gitignored — a blank clone ships without vectors.'

README PUTS THE DISK COST OUTSIDE THE FOLDER; THE SCRIPTS PUT MOST OF IT INSIDE. README.md:72: 'its dictionary is kept outside the folder, in a service area of your system — about one gigabyte.' In fact the ~1 GB is the venv at .memory_venv/ INSIDE the folder (memory_index_setup.sh:5, memory-embedding-layer.md:113) and only the ~309 MB model cache is outside, under ~/.cache/huggingface (memory_index_setup.sh:29-30). The presentation gets this right — 'It sits partly in your folder and partly in your system's hidden downloads area' (presentation:114) — so the README contradicts its own sibling document.

THE RESTORE PROMISE HAS NO ROUTE. docs/en/presentation.md:66 ('earlier versions of the files are kept, so anything can be brought back') and :141 ('the safety net of earlier versions of your notes'), plus README.md:31, promise recovery. No file in the folder documents how: there is no git log / checkout / revert step in any skill, hook, script or doc, and the only recovery actually written down is manual folder-swapping (presentation:134).

THE SAVE THRESHOLD IS TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS. CLAUDE.md:45 sets the budget at '60K target · 100K ceiling → /session-save'; session-save/SKILL.md:3 and :9 say 'when context exceeds 150K tokens'; compress/SKILL.md:66 splits the difference, citing both the '100K ceiling' and 'the ~150K session-save threshold' in one paragraph.

THE ENTRY COMMAND IS SPELLED BOTH WAYS. CLAUDE.md:5 and HOME.md:9 tell the person to type `start` with no slash, and session-start.sh:23 accepts either; README.md:40 and docs/en/presentation.md:30 tell them to type `/start` with the slash ('with the slash… The last thing you need to know'). start/SKILL.md:178 says 'start is the only thing they type' while :35 lists the commands as `/start`.

SELF-CHECK LOOKS FOR A CLAUDE.md SECTION THAT ISN'T THERE. self-check/SKILL.md:20 checks for the sections 'Identity/Rules, Context, Orchestration, Hard rules, Naming'. The shipped CLAUDE.md has Rules, Boot, Scope-gate, Orchestration, Memory, Budget, Hard rules, Self-improvement, Architecture — there is no 'Context' section and no 'Naming' section (naming is hard rule 4 at CLAUDE.md:51).

/reflect IS ADVERTISED WITH A FEATURE IT DOESN'T HAVE. docs/en/presentation.md:98 describes /reflect as also showing you 'what it has understood about your manner and what it still does not know'. reflect/SKILL.md has no step that shows the person anything of the kind — Step 6 writes reports/reflection-{date}.md and the identity/manner candidates are written to files, not presented as a read-back (reflect:39, 66-69).

publish.sh BRANCH ASSUMPTION IS MAINTAINER-ONLY AND WILL FAIL ELSEWHERE. scripts/publish.sh:11 hard-fails unless the current branch is `main` and force-pushes a derived `gitee` branch; it also uses BSD `sed -i ''` (publish.sh:18,26,37), which fails on GNU sed — i.e. on the Linux the README:29 names as a supported platform. It ships in a folder whose own rule says git here is local-only with 'no shared remote' (rules/local-only-repo.md:14-16).
